# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  RUBRIC DEFINITION - Sensors for Creative Technology
#  Assignment 6: Magnetic Sensing - Hall-effect rotary position sensor
#  (two linear Hall sensors + magnet wheel, potentiometer as reference)
#  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  Total points: 30
#  EU grade: 1 + 9 x (earned / 30)
#
#  1. Introduction         3 pt  (1+1+1)
#  2. Analysis             7 pt  (1+1+1+2+2)
#  3. Method & setup       6 pt  (1+2+1+1+1)
#  4. Results              5 pt  (1+1+1+1+1)
#  5. Conclusion           6 pt  (1+1+1+1+1+1)
#  6. Format & structure   3 pt  (2+1)
#
#  Same architecture as the Assignment 3 rubric: every criterion = one
#  slider (the points) + one observation checklist (points_per_positive: 0,
#  so it only generates feedback text and never changes the score).
#  Use the notes under the checklist for the Canvas 'Comment' field.
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

title: "Sensors - Hall-effect rotation sensor (Assignment 6)"
course: "SCT-A6"
grading: true
grade_decimals: 1

sections:

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 1. INTRODUCTION  ·  3 pt  (1+1+1)
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - id: intro
    title: "introduction"
    fields:

      - id: intro_type
        label: "introduction - sensor type (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "Is the correct sensor type mentioned? (Two linear, ratiometric Hall-effect sensors (A1302 or similar) read out with a wheel of alternating magnets, and a potentiometer as reference.)"

      - id: intro_type_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "sensor type missing or vague (only 'an angle sensor')"
          - "only the Hall sensors, or only the potentiometer, named"
          - "wrong sensor type (e.g. optical encoder, or a Hall switch / latch instead of a linear Hall sensor)"
        positive:
          - "linear (ratiometric) Hall-effect sensor named, together with the magnet wheel"
          - "potentiometer named as the reference"

      - id: intro_principle
        label: "introduction - physical principle (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "Is the physical measurement principle mentioned?"

      - id: intro_principle_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "no physical principle mentioned"
          - "principle given for only one of the two sensors (Hall or potentiometer)"
          - "describes the electronics or the process instead of the physics"
        positive:
          - "Hall effect: a magnetic field gives an output voltage proportional to the flux density"
          - "two sensors with a 90 degree phase difference give a sine / cosine pair from which the angle follows"
          - "potentiometer: wiper voltage proportional to the angle"

      - id: intro_goal
        label: "introduction - measurement goal (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "Is the goal clearly stated, without irrelevant (process-related) information?"

      - id: intro_goal_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "goal missing or unclear"
          - "goal buried in a description of what was done or which hardware was handed out"
          - "goal is only 'to do the assignment'"
        positive:
          - "goal stated in one or two sentences (implement and characterise the Hall-effect angle sensor with the potentiometer as reference)"
          - "properties to be determined are named (angular range, resolution, precision, accuracy)"

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 2. ANALYSIS  ·  7 pt  (1+1+1+2+2)
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - id: analysis
    title: "analysis"
    fields:

      - id: an_measurand
        label: "analysis - measurand (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "It is clearly described what is measured: which physical quantity and in which units. Reference: the rotation angle of the wheel (mechanical angle, in degrees) over the total range (270 to 280 degrees). One magnet transition (one wave) is 360 electrical degrees, which is two magnet pitches: 67.5 degrees for the 33.75 degree pitch of the wheel (9 magnets spread over 270 degrees; 360/9 = 40 degrees is not the pitch), so electrical and mechanical angle must not be mixed up."

      - id: an_measurand_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "measurand not named"
          - "mechanical and electrical angle mixed up (a transition is 360 electrical degrees, not 360 mechanical degrees)"
          - "only raw ADC counts or volts, no angle unit"
          - "degrees and radians mixed, or units inconsistent between text and graphs"
        positive:
          - "measurand named explicitly (rotation angle of the wheel)"
          - "unit stated (degrees) with the relation between electrical and mechanical angle (360 electrical degrees = 2 magnet pitches = 67.5 degrees for 9 magnets over 270 degrees)"
          - "same units used throughout text and graphs"

      - id: an_principle
        label: "analysis - physical principle (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The physical principle used for the sensor is described concisely and correctly: Hall effect with magnets of alternating polarity, a linear ratiometric output around half the supply voltage, and why two sensors with a phase offset give a sine / cosine pair. Note: part of this text is pre-filled in the template, so look for the student's own explanation."

      - id: an_principle_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "only the pre-filled template text, no own explanation"
          - "alternating polarity of the magnets not mentioned, so the period per transition is unexplained"
          - "Hall sensor described wrongly (e.g. output proportional to the magnet position, or a switching output instead of a linear one)"
          - "phase difference not explained (sensor distance versus magnet distance, see the figure with D_sensor and D_magnet)"
          - "not concise (copied datasheet text)"
        positive:
          - "output voltage proportional to the field through the sensor, quiescent output at half the supply, ratiometric"
          - "magnets alternate N / S, so one transition (360 electrical degrees) spans two magnet pitches"
          - "sensor spacing equals one transition plus 90 degrees, which gives the sine / cosine pair"
          - "concise and correct"

      - id: an_reference
        label: "analysis - the reference (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The reference used to characterise the sensor is discussed, including its operating principle and its limits. Reference values (Alps RK09K1130AH1, taper B = linear): 10 kOhm, wiper voltage proportional to the angle; mechanical travel 280 +/- 5 degrees; the taper curve in the datasheet is flat near 0 % below about 28 degrees and near 100 % above about 252 degrees (nominal electrical range about 224 degrees), and the datasheet only guarantees 40-60 % at 140 degrees; comparing the wave period of the wheel (67.5 degrees) with the apparent period on a 280 degree scale gives an electrical range of about 225-235 degrees, in line with the curve; read with the 10-bit ADC, 0.27 degrees per count if 280 degrees is assumed. Strict reading (Edwin, 2026-11-03): the point is only given when the electrical range is recognised as different from the mechanical travel (nominal 28 to 252 degrees) and used (in the conversion, the usable range or the limits); a description with the mechanical 280 degrees only earns 0, also when the wiper principle is explained."

      - id: an_reference_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "reference mentioned but operating principle not explained (resistive divider with a wiper)"
          - "potentiometer specifications missing or wrong (electrical angle, resistance, taper)"
          - "no discussion of the limits of the reference (electrical versus mechanical angle, linearity tolerance, ADC resolution)"
          - "no discussion of how the potentiometer angle is aligned with the wheel angle (zero offset, angle range)"
        positive:
          - "wiper of the 10 kOhm potentiometer as a voltage divider explained"
          - "specifications quoted correctly with source (mechanical travel 280 degrees, electrical range, linear taper)"
          - "reference limitations mentioned (electrical range smaller than the mechanical travel, flat output at both ends, 0.25 degrees per ADC count, linearity)"
          - "alignment of the two angle scales discussed"

      - id: an_equations
        label: "analysis - relevant equations (2 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 2
        step: 1
        points: 2
        description: "The equations from physical quantity, to electrical signal (voltage), to value in degrees (software), for both the sensor and the reference. Reference values (A1302, 1.3 mV/G; an A1301 has 2.5 mV/G, so twice the swing; both types are in use and students have to check which one they have): about 480 G at the sensor (field calculator, N45 magnet 4 x 1.5 mm) x 1.3 mV/G = about 0.62 V swing around 2.5 V = about 245 ADC counts peak-to-peak (a quarter of the ADC range); x = (A4 - mid) / amplitude, y = (A5 - mid) / amplitude; theta_el = atan2(y, x); unwrapping by adding or subtracting 360 at every jump; theta = summed electrical angle x 270 / 1440 (67.5 degrees per wave, 4 transitions for 9 magnets over 270 degrees); reference angle = 280 x ADC / 1023 (or 28 + 224 x ADC / 1023 for the nominal electrical range)."

      - id: an_equations_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "no chain from field to voltage to ADC count to angle"
          - "equations only for one of the two sensors"
          - "arctan(y / x) used where atan2 is needed (quadrant lost), or the two signals swapped or not offset-corrected"
          - "transition counting (unwrapping) not given"
          - "scaling from summed electrical angle to mechanical angle missing or inverted (multiply versus divide)"
          - "expected voltage swing from sensitivity and field calculator not given"
          - "template placeholders left empty ([n], [deg], [mV/gauss])"
        positive:
          - "sensitivity and field combined to the expected swing in mV and in ADC counts, compared with the measured swing (right sensitivity for the sensor type: A1301 2.5 mV/G, A1302 1.3 mV/G)"
          - "angle within one transition from atan2 of the two offset-corrected signals"
          - "unwrapping rule and scaling to mechanical degrees correct and consistent with the code"
          - "reference angle equation with the datasheet value of the potentiometer"
          - "all values with units"

      - id: an_conditioning
        label: "analysis - conditioning (2 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 2
        step: 1
        points: 2
        description: "The circuits used for conditioning the sensor signals are described: supply and output of the Hall sensors, the potentiometer divider, the ADC inputs (A4, A5, A0). The expected use of the ADC range is discussed (the signals only occupy a small part of 0-5 V) and the offset and amplitude correction (centre at 2.5 V, normalisation) is explained. The used components are shown in the schematic. Strict reading: 2 points need the centre and amplitude of each sensor determined from the data (not a fixed 512) together with the used ADC range compared with the expected swing; with a fixed 512 at most 1."

      - id: an_conditioning_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "schematic missing, or template specimen left in"
          - "components or pin numbers (A4, A5, A0) not labelled"
          - "only one of the two signal paths shown (Hall sensors or potentiometer)"
          - "fraction of the ADC range that is used not estimated"
          - "offset (2.5 V centre) and amplitude not discussed, a fixed value of 512 assumed without comment"
          - "figure not referenced in the text"
        positive:
          - "schematic shows both Hall sensors on A4 and A5 and the potentiometer on A0"
          - "component values and designators match the text"
          - "expected swing compared with the ADC range and with the measured swing (about 245 of 1023 counts for an A1302)"
          - "ratiometric output read by a ratiometric ADC (supply variations cancel), and tolerance of quiescent output and sensitivity mentioned"
          - "figure referenced where discussed"
          - "centre and amplitude of each sensor determined from the data (min / max) and checked with the Lissajous plot"

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 3. METHOD & SETUP  ·  6 pt  (1+2+1+1+1)
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - id: method
    title: "method & setup"
    fields:

      - id: me_setup
        label: "method - setup (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The setup is described: physical aspects (the wheel with its number of magnets and their spacing, the distance between magnets and sensors, how the wheel is turned, where the potentiometer sits), location of the used components on the shield, and the setting of the experiment. Strict reading: the room temperature has to be mentioned (a value or explicitly room temperature, with the place); a desk or table without temperature earns 0."

      - id: me_setup_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "no physical description (wheel, magnets, air gap, how it is rotated)"
          - "shield drawing missing, generic, or used parts not marked"
          - "number of magnets, spacing or air gap not stated"
          - "experiment conditions (room temperature and place) not mentioned; a desk without temperature is not enough"
          - "no photo or sketch of the wheel and the magnet placement"
        positive:
          - "annotated shield drawing marking the Hall sensors and the potentiometer"
          - "wheel drawing or photo with the number of magnets, spacing (33.75 degrees pitch for 9 magnets over 270 degrees) and air gap"
          - "conditions stated (room, approximate temperature, table)"
          - "how the wheel was turned (by hand, slowly) described"

      - id: me_code
        label: "method - code (2 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 2
        step: 1
        points: 2
        description: "The code used for the experiment is described and given. Concise, cleaned-up and minimal; copy-pasting from the reader is not the way to go. The code outputs the computed angle and the reference angle. Strict reading: 2 points need floats throughout, text and code in agreement, and constants traceable to data; an angle stored as int (truncation to whole degrees, which then propagates into the reported resolution), or a mismatch between text and code, caps the score at 1."

      - id: me_code_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "code copied from the reader or wiki without cleaning"
          - "long listing with unused parts or no comments"
          - "constants or formulas in the code do not match the text (offset, scaling 270/1440, atan2 argument order)"
          - "code for the angle or for the reference conversion missing (a conversion done in a spreadsheet is accepted when the formula and constants are stated explicitly, but belongs in the code eventually)"
          - "no unwrapping (transition counting) in the code"
          - "listing formatted poorly (large white space, unreadable)"
          - "angle stored as int (truncation to whole degrees), which propagates into the reported resolution"
        positive:
          - "short listing covering both conversions (Hall angle and potentiometer angle per line)"
          - "unwrapping and scaling visible and matching the text"
          - "constants (centre, amplitude, scale) traceable to the data"
          - "code explained in the text (what it does, sample rate)"

      - id: me_reference
        label: "method - reference (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The reference signal, reference measurement or calibration source is described."

      - id: me_reference_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "no description of how the potentiometer angle is obtained (range, offset)"
          - "zero position of wheel and potentiometer not aligned, or the alignment not described"
          - "potentiometer range taken from the datasheet without checking it against the wheel range"
          - "'calibrated' claimed without any data"
        positive:
          - "potentiometer conversion with the angle range from the datasheet (280 degrees mechanical, or the electrical range if recognised)"
          - "alignment (offset and scale) of the reference and the sensor angle determined from the data"
          - "accuracy or resolution of the reference mentioned (0.25 degrees per count, linearity)"

      - id: me_samples
        label: "method - samples (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The number of samples, measurements or series taken is stated."

      - id: me_samples_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "number of swings or samples not stated"
          - "only a single swing"
          - "sampling interval / rate not mentioned"
          - "no static points or sorted data for the precision"
        positive:
          - "number of swings and direction (up and down) stated"
          - "sample rate stated"
          - "enough swings to see repeatability (3 or more)"
          - "number of samples behind the precision value stated"

      - id: me_procedure
        label: "method - procedure (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The steps taken, and in which order, are described."

      - id: me_procedure_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "steps not in order or not reproducible"
          - "rotation speed or direction not described"
          - "unclear how the starting position and the transition count were initialised"
          - "end stops of the potentiometer or the wheel range not mentioned"
        positive:
          - "ordered steps from raw signals to calibrated angle"
          - "slow, repeated swings over the full range, in both directions"
          - "starting position and initial segment defined"
          - "precision measured at fixed angles (holds) or by sorting the data"

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 4. RESULTS  ·  5 pt  (1+1+1+1+1)
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - id: results
    title: "results"
    fields:

      - id: re_time
        label: "results - time series (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "A clear graph showing the experimental procedure: the raw values of the two Hall sensors and the potentiometer in time over a number of swings, corresponding to the outlined procedure. The raw values show how much of the ADC range is used."

      - id: re_time_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "no time series of the raw values shown"
          - "swings not recognisable"
          - "time axis in sample number only, or not in seconds"
          - "raw counts and degrees on one unlabelled axis"
          - "the two Hall signals not distinguishable"
        positive:
          - "raw A4, A5 and potentiometer in one graph, clear swings"
          - "time axis in seconds"
          - "used part of the ADC range visible (about 400-600 counts)"
          - "corresponds to the described procedure"

      - id: re_calibration
        label: "results - calibration graph (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "A clear graph showing sensor data and reference data. A time series can be added, but the important one is the x-y graph of the calculated angle versus the potentiometer angle."

      - id: re_calibration_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "no x-y plot, only time series"
          - "axes swapped (reference belongs on x)"
          - "no ideal line (y = x) to judge the deviation"
          - "unlabelled axes or units"
          - "offset between the two angle scales not corrected"
        positive:
          - "x-y plot: calculated angle versus reference angle, in degrees"
          - "ideal line drawn"
          - "several swings visible"
          - "calculated angle and reference also shown in one time series"

      - id: re_error
        label: "results - error plot (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "A clear graph showing the error (difference between reference and measured value). The reference angle range on the x-axis is better than the time series."

      - id: re_error_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "no error plot"
          - "error plotted against time instead of against the reference angle"
          - "error definition or sign not stated"
          - "edges of the range (where the reference saturates) not commented"
        positive:
          - "error versus reference angle, in degrees"
          - "valid range indicated, or the edges explained"
          - "sign convention stated"
          - "periodic pattern with the magnet pitch visible or discussed"

      - id: re_nonlinear
        label: "results - non-ideal details (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "Graphs showing relevant details of non-ideal behaviour: the x-y (Lissajous) plot of the two Hall signals (a circle when offsets, amplitudes and the 90 degree phase are right), the error within one magnet transition, or a close-up showing the resolution steps. (Hysteresis is not asked in this assignment.)"

      - id: re_nonlinear_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "non-ideal behaviour claimed (bumps, edge errors) but not shown"
          - "no x-y plot of the two Hall signals"
          - "no close-up of one or two transitions"
          - "bumps visible in the angle but not analysed"
        positive:
          - "Lissajous plot of A4 against A5 showing offset, ellipse or distortion"
          - "close-up of a few transitions with the error pattern"
          - "close-up of the angle steps at slow rotation (resolution)"

      - id: re_graphing
        label: "results - graphing quality (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The graphs show a relevant number of samples, have good scaling, and relevant (SI) units on the axes (degrees, seconds, counts or volts)."

      - id: re_graphing_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "axis titles or units missing (default chart titles)"
          - "raw counts and angles mixed on one axis"
          - "poor scaling, or too few samples"
          - "units not consistent with the text (degrees versus radians, electrical versus mechanical)"
        positive:
          - "all axes labelled with units"
          - "sensible scaling and enough samples"
          - "units consistent with the text"

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 5. CONCLUSION  ·  6 pt  (1+1+1+1+1+1)
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - id: conclusion
    title: "conclusion"
    fields:

      - id: co_accuracy
        label: "conclusion - accuracy (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "A meaningful and quantified notion of accuracy, linked to the angular range of the sensor. The accuracy of the reference is discussed too. The mean and standard deviation of the error tell only part of the story: look for the worst-case error, and the error in the middle of the range versus the edges. Strict reading: the point needs the RMS or worst-case error in degrees plus at least one of a percentage of the range or a (quantitative) remark on the accuracy of the reference; both missing earns 0."

      - id: co_accuracy_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "accuracy given only as the mean error (close to zero by symmetry)"
          - "no link to the range (no percentage of the 270 degrees)"
          - "accuracy of the reference (linearity, ADC step, electrical angle) not discussed"
          - "edge errors (outside the valid reference range) included without comment"
        positive:
          - "worst-case or RMS error in degrees and as percentage of the range"
          - "accuracy of the reference discussed (potentiometer linearity: the datasheet only guarantees 40-60 % at mid travel; about 0.25 degrees per count)"
          - "range over which the number holds is stated"
          - "error without the edge region also given"

      - id: co_resolution
        label: "conclusion - resolution (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "A meaningful, quantified notion of resolution, for both the reference and the sensor signal. Pay attention to the voltage range that the Hall sensors actually use. Reference: potentiometer 225 to 280 degrees / 1023 = 0.22 to 0.27 degrees per count (electrical or mechanical range); Hall signals: a swing of about 245 counts (a quarter of the ADC range); a single-signal estimate gives 270 / 960 = 0.28 degrees; with two signals and atan2 the electrical resolution is about 1 / A radians (A = amplitude in counts, about 120), which is about 0.1 mechanical degrees. A value that is an artefact of integer truncation or of print rounding (1 degree, 0.1 or 0.01 degrees) is not a resolution and earns 0."

      - id: co_resolution_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "resolution only as ADC bits or counts, not translated to degrees"
          - "voltage range actually used (about 0.6 V around 2.5 V) not taken into account: 10 bit assumed over the full range"
          - "no value for the Hall angle, or none for the reference"
          - "resolution of the reference not compared with that of the sensor"
          - "single-signal estimate used without discussing the effect of combining two signals"
        positive:
          - "reference resolution in degrees per count (about 0.25 degrees)"
          - "used ADC range translated into degrees per count for the Hall signals"
          - "effective resolution with atan2 derived or measured from the data (smallest step at slow rotation)"
          - "limit of the reference as measurement instrument mentioned"

      - id: co_precision
        label: "conclusion - precision (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "Precision can be calculated from multiple measurements of the same thing (the same angle), giving a (standard) deviation. The standard deviation of the error is related, but repeated readings at fixed angles, or the sorted data at a number of angles, is better. Strict reading: precision needs holds, or turning to a certain position and returning to it repeatedly; the spread of the error over a sweep, or the repeatability of repeated sweeps, is not precision and earns 0 unless a hold is analysed."

      - id: co_precision_obs
        label: "observations"
        type: checklist
        points_per_positive: 0
        negative:
          - "precision confused with accuracy (standard deviation of the error over the whole range called precision)"
          - "no repeated measurement at the same angle"
          - "standard deviation of the error given without noting its limitation (it contains systematic errors per transition)"
        positive:
          - "standard deviation of repeated readings at fixed angles (static holds) or of sorted data per angle bin"
          - "noise in ADC counts translated into degrees"
          - "number of samples behind the value stated"

      - id: co_range
        label: "conclusion - range (1 pt)"
        type: slider
        min: 0
        max: 1
        step: 1
        points: 1
        description: "The relevant input and output ranges are stated in meaningful units: the angular range of the sensor (270 to 280 degrees, with number of magnets and transitions), the range of the reference, and the output voltage range of the Hall sensors. If the behaviour is only valid in a certain range, this is mentioned. Strict reading: the electrical range of the reference (smaller than its mechanical travel) has to be stated for the point; the mechanical 280 degrees alone is not enough."

      - id: co_range_obs

values.intro_principle_obs__pos_note: Hall sensors evaluate differences in the magnetic field, and the two signals have a 90 degree phase shift from which the angle follows.
values.intro_goal_obs__neg_note: The properties to determine (accuracy, precision, resolution, range) are not named.
values.intro_goal_obs__pos_note: The goal is to establish a rotary position sensor and confirm it against the potentiometer.
values.an_measurand_obs__neg_note: The relation between the electrical angle per magnet transition and the wheel angle (67.5 degrees per wave for 9 magnets over 270 degrees) is not given. Borderline.
values.an_measurand_obs__pos_note: The measurand is the rotational angle in degrees.
values.an_principle_obs__neg_note: The Analysis only has the template text; the alternating polarity of the magnets and the reason for the phase difference (sensor spacing versus magnet spacing) are not explained.
values.an_reference_obs__neg_note: Strict reading: the potentiometer is described with its mechanical 280 degrees only (+ 5); the flattening of the plot around 260-280 degrees is attributed to the sensor (the sensor can no longer resolve variations in angle), while it is the potentiometer that flattens (the end of its electrical range, nominal 28 to 252 degrees on the datasheet curve). Name and use the electrical range for the reference.
values.an_reference_obs__pos_note: Datasheet range (280 + 5 degrees) quoted with source.
values.an_equations_obs__neg_note: The expected swing (514 G x 1.3 mV/G = 668 mV) is not given in ADC counts and not compared with the measured swing; the formulas in the text are hard to read (garbled), and the comment in the sketch about 1695 is a leftover.
values.an_equations_obs__pos_note: Expected swing from field and sensitivity, atan2 of the offset-corrected signals, unwrapping, a calibration from the 0 degree and 280 degree readings (98 and -1041), and the reference equation.
values.an_conditioning_obs__neg_note: The circuits are not described and the used part of the ADC range is not estimated; the signals use almost the full range (Fig. 10), which should be compared with the expected 668 mV swing.
values.an_conditioning_obs__pos_note: Schematic with both Hall sensors and the potentiometer; the centre of 512 counts (2.5 V) is stated.
values.me_setup_obs__neg_note: No photo or drawing of the wheel with the magnets and the air gap.
values.me_setup_obs__pos_note: Shield drawing with the used parts, and the conditions (stable table, inside, 22 degrees C, wheel turned slowly by hand).
values.me_code_obs__neg_note: The sketch is mostly the wiki code with leftover comments (supply yours!, 1695 is the calibrated value) and a mismatch with the calibration actually used. alpha_deg is an int, which truncates the angle to whole degrees and sets the resolution of 1 degree that you report; use a float. The sample rate (delay(20)) is not stated.
values.me_code_obs__pos_note: Both angles (Hall and reference) are printed per line, with unwrapping and a two-point calibration.
values.me_reference_obs__pos_note: Potentiometer converted with 280 degrees, and the Hall angle aligned with it using the readings at 0 and 280 degrees.
values.me_samples_obs__neg_note: The sample rate and the number of samples are not stated.
values.me_samples_obs__pos_note: Three turns from 0 to 280 degrees.
values.me_procedure_obs__pos_note: The wheel is turned to 0 degrees before the code starts, then three slow turns; the phase difference is recorded over three turns and plotted in Excel.
values.re_time_obs__neg_note: The time axis is in sample number, and the raw plot in degrees (Fig. 6) is not the raw ADC value.
values.re_time_obs__pos_note: Raw A4, A5 and potentiometer values in one graph (Fig. 10) over three turns.
values.re_calibration_obs__neg_note: Check that Fig. 8 has the ideal line (y = x), and state the axes in the caption (the caption says degrees against degrees).
values.re_calibration_obs__pos_note: Calibrated angle against reference angle (Fig. 8) with the periodic deviation visible.
values.re_error_obs__neg_note: The error plot is described with the samples on the x-axis; plot it against the reference angle and state the sign (Fig. 9 shows about +10 to -18 degrees, the text gives a worst case of 10.6 degrees).
values.re_error_obs__pos_note: An error plot showing the periodic error.
values.re_nonlinear_obs__neg_note: Fig. 11 (both raw signals against the reference angle, showing the flattening of phase A near 230 degrees) is a useful detail, but a Lissajous plot (A5 against A4) and a close-up of one or two waves would show the shape and the phase directly. Borderline.
values.re_graphing_obs__neg_note: Figure labels and captions in brackets and some caption texts do not describe the axes correctly.
values.re_graphing_obs__pos_note: Axes with units in the plots.
values.co_accuracy_obs__neg_note: The numbers do not agree with your own plots: the mean error is -4.9 degrees and the mean absolute error is also 4.9 degrees, which is only possible if all errors are negative, while Fig. 9 shows the error oscillating between +10 and -18 degrees (a mean absolute error of about 8 degrees); the worst case of 10.6 degrees is below the -18 degrees in Fig. 9. The full-scale percentage (1.75 %) follows from the wrong mean absolute error. Check the calculation (RMS and worst case in degrees and as a percentage of the range), and quantify the accuracy of the reference.
values.co_accuracy_obs__pos_note: A full-scale percentage is attempted, and the cause (calibration) is named.
values.co_resolution_obs__neg_note: The resolution of 1 degree is the effect of the int type in the sketch (the lowest non-zero difference between cells), not of the sensor. The resolution of the Hall angle follows from the amplitude of the signals (about 400-500 counts, so about 0.1 degrees electrical, 0.03 degrees of rotation), and the reference gives 280/1023 = 0.27 degrees per count.
values.co_precision_obs__neg_note: Strict reading: precision needs holds, or turning to a certain position and returning to it repeatedly. The standard deviation of the error over three cycles (6.5 degrees) is mostly accuracy; you note that it includes hysteresis and calibration effects, which is correct.
values.co_range_obs__neg_note: Strict reading: only the mechanical range (0-280 degrees) is stated; the electrical range of the reference has to be stated, and the signal swing of the Hall sensors is not given.
values.co_nonlin_obs__neg_note: No comparison with an expectation (datasheet) and the flattening near 260-280 degrees is attributed to the sensor, while the potentiometer is also flat near its ends (datasheet curve).
values.co_nonlin_obs__pos_note: Periodic error of about +10 to -18 degrees, the flattening at the end, and the flattening of phase A near 230 degrees.
values.co_improve_obs__neg_note: A third Hall sensor at 120 degrees is not supported by the data and the reasoning (the sine waves cancel to a flat line) is not correct; a correction of the centre, amplitude and phase of the two signals, or a look-up table, would address the periodic error directly.
values.co_improve_obs__pos_note: The bottleneck is identified from the data: the repeating wave in the error.
values.fo_template_obs__neg_note: Figure labels with brackets, figure numbers used inconsistently in the text (Figure 6 for two different plots), garbled formulas and a caption text that is not a sentence.
values.fo_references_obs__pos_note: A reference list: figures and equations from the wiki, code adapted from the wiki, the A1302 datasheet, and footnotes for the datasheets and the calculator.
values.overall_note: A complete report with a sound set of results: a two-point calibration from the 0 and 280 degree readings, accuracy given as mean, mean absolute and worst case with the full-scale percentage (1.75 %), three turns, a Fig. 11 that shows the raw signals against the angle, and a reference list. Points to improve: (1) the resolution of 1 degree is caused by the int type of alpha_deg: use a float and derive the resolution from the amplitude of the signals (about 0.03 degrees) and the ADC step of the reference (0.27 degrees); (2) the worst case in the text (10.6 degrees) does not match Fig. 9 (-18 degrees); (3) static holds at fixed angles for the precision; (4) a Lissajous plot to show the offset, amplitude and phase of the two signals, and a correction of these instead of a third sensor; (5) the principle in the Analysis (alternating magnets, phase from the sensor spacing), the electrical range of the potentiometer (the flattening near 260-280 degrees is the reference), a photo or drawing of the wheel, and clean up the sketch comments from the wiki.

values.me_reference_obs__pos_note: Potentiometer converted with 280 degrees.
values.me_samples_obs__neg_note: The sample rate and the number of samples are not stated.
values.me_samples_obs__pos_note: Three full turns of 280 degrees.

values.re_time_obs__neg_note: The raw signals are plotted against the angle (Fig. 7) and not against time; the time axis in Fig. 4 is in sample number.
values.re_time_obs__pos_note: Calibrated and reference angle over three turns (Fig. 4).
values.re_calibration_obs__neg_note: No ideal line (y = x) in Fig. 5, which would show directly that the slope is wrong.
values.re_calibration_obs__pos_note: Calibrated angle against reference angle (Fig. 5).
values.re_error_obs__neg_note: The sign of the error is not stated, and the growing error (up to about 85 degrees at 230 degrees) is not commented: it is a wrong slope in the calibration, not noise.
values.re_error_obs__pos_note: Error against the reference angle (Fig. 6).
values.re_nonlinear_obs__neg_note: Fig. 7 shows the raw phases against the angle (including a flat part at the end) but this is not analysed; add a Lissajous plot (A5 against A4) and a close-up of one wave.
values.re_graphing_obs__neg_note: The captions of Fig. 6 and Fig. 7 are the same and do not describe Fig. 7 (phase A and phase B over reference).
values.re_graphing_obs__pos_note: Axis titles with units in the plots.
values.co_accuracy_obs__neg_note: An accuracy of 31.5 is given without a unit or a definition, and the reference is said to have an accuracy of 0, which is not correct (the potentiometer has a tolerance, a resolution of 0.27 degrees and an electrical range of 26 to 254 degrees). Give the worst case or RMS error in degrees and as a percentage of the range.
values.co_resolution_obs__neg_note: The resolution of 0.274 degrees (280/1023) is that of the potentiometer, not of the Hall sensor. The Hall angle resolution follows from the amplitude of the signals (about 450 counts, so about 0.13 degrees electrical, 0.03 degrees of rotation).
values.co_precision_obs__neg_note: A standard deviation of 27.83 (no unit) over the whole range is the spread of a large calibration error, not precision; use repeated readings at fixed angles (static holds). The precision of the reference is not 0.
values.co_range_obs__neg_note: The output swing of the Hall sensors in volts or counts is not stated.
values.co_range_obs__pos_note: Mechanical range 0-280 degrees, electrical range 26-254 degrees (from the datasheet curve), and a measured range of -2 to 317 degrees.
values.co_nonlin_obs__neg_note: The oscillation in the error is attributed to gaps between magnets, but no numbers (period, peak-to-peak) are given and the dominant error (a growing slope up to about 85 degrees) is a calibration error.
values.co_improve_obs__neg_note: The conclusion that the magnet was faulty is not supported by data (it is said to follow from comparing with other students); the main bottleneck in your data is the calibration constant (about 1185 instead of 920), which a least-squares fit of the unwrapped Hall angle against the reference would give. Adding magnets is not linked to the results.
values.fo_template_obs__neg_note: Template text is left in (270 [deg] phase difference, 31.1 degrees apart), and the captions of Fig. 6 and Fig. 7 are the same.
values.fo_template_obs__pos_note: All sections present; figures numbered.
values.fo_references_obs__pos_note: Datasheets (sensor, magnet, potentiometer) and the field calculator referenced, and the wiki schematic credited.
values.overall_note: A report that follows the structure and records good raw data (Fig. 7 shows clean sinusoidal signals, the electrical range of the potentiometer is acknowledged: 26 to 254 degrees), but the calibration is wrong and nothing in the analysis checks it: the scale 270/920 equals 105 degrees per wave, while the data shows about 82 degrees per wave (about 1185 instead of 920), which explains the error of up to 85 degrees. Points to improve: (1) fit the unwrapped Hall angle against the reference (slope and offset) and plot the result with the ideal line; (2) the Analysis: the principle (Hall effect, alternating magnets, phase from sensor spacing) and remove the template values (270 degrees, 31.1 degrees); (3) accuracy as worst case or RMS in degrees and percent of the range, resolution from the amplitude of the signals (about 0.03 degrees), and precision from static holds; (4) a Lissajous plot of the two signals before concluding that the magnet was faulty; (5) the conditions of the experiment and a photo or drawing of the wheel.

values.intro_goal_obs__pos_note: Clear goal: usable range, resolution, accuracy and precision against the potentiometer.

The expected swing is not given in counts.
values.an_equations_obs__pos_note: Expected swing worked out (1500 G x 2.5 mV/G = 3.75 V) with the conclusion that the outputs clip, atan2, unwrapping, scale -5.519 and offset -216.6, and the reference equation, all matching the sketch.

values.co_accuracy_obs__pos_note: The usable range over which the numbers hold (5 to 218 degrees) is stated.
values.co_resolution_obs__pos_note: Reference 0.22 degrees per count and about 0.03 degrees per count for the Hall angle, not uniform because of the clipping.
values.co_precision_obs__pos_note: Standard deviation of 0.23, 0.34 and 0.18 degrees at three holds (average 0.25 degrees).
values.co_range_obs__pos_note: Usable range 5 to 218 degrees of the 224 degree electrical range of the potentiometer.
values.co_nonlin_obs__pos_note: Repeating error with a period of 30-35 degrees explained by the 134 degree phase and the clipping.
values.co_improve_obs__pos_note: Concrete options: a 90 degree phase mechanically or in software, and a larger magnet-to-sensor distance against the clipping.

values.fo_references_obs__pos_note: Numbered references: sensor and magnet datasheets, the field calculator, the potentiometer datasheet and the course page.

Points to improve: (1) a Lissajous plot of A5 against A4 and a close-up of one wave; (2) the maximum error as a percentage of the range and the accuracy of the reference; (3) the conditions of the experiment (room temperature) and a drawing of the wheel, and the maximum error as a percentage of the range with the accuracy of the reference; (4) centre and amplitude of each sensor instead of a fixed 512.
